interface.title: Chemometric Workbench (RUO)
interface.field: Analytical chemistry / chemometrics (NIR-like spectra, PFAS concentration panels)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory data analysis, quality control and calibration modelling of measured analytical data
interface.what_it_is_for: A Streamlit app for research and training use. A chemist loads a sample-by-feature table, picks a preprocessing method and explores it with PCA. They flag outlier samples with Hotelling's T² and Q-residual limits, fit a cross-validated PLS regression to a numeric target, and check feature influence, applicability domain and uncertainty before exporting CSVs and the fitted model.
interface.note: The About tab (screens/042.webp) lists the methods (T² limits from the F-distribution, Q limits from Jackson-Mudholkar), a roadmap (SHAP panel, batch anomaly detection, LC-MS/MS QA module) and a governance line: research-use-only, not EPA/ISO certified.

data.note: Most of the work used the built-in 'Synthetic spectral demo' (120 samples × 200 wavelength columns 1000–2500 nm, plus group, target and a hidden _injected_outlier column). I also regenerated it once with 180 samples and seed 8. I uploaded the test file example_pfas_panel.csv (20 samples, groups A/B, about 10 PFAS analyte columns, a missing PFOS value in S008). With the default column set it crashed (see not_done). It ran only after I cut the feature list down to PFOA, PFHxS, PFNA, PFBS and PFOS. With those, S015 was flagged as a T² outlier and S008 as a Q outlier (screens/056.webp).

features.name: Preprocessing selector that drives the whole analysis
features.general: Pick a signal pretreatment from a list and see every downstream plot, flag and model metric recomputed, so methods can be compared side by side
features.specific: Sidebar 'Preprocessing' select (none, mean-center, autoscale, SNV, MSC, Savitzky-Golay smooth, Savitzky-Golay 1st derivative). It feeds the scree, score and loading plots, the T²/Q limits and the PLS fit
steps: open the Preprocessing dropdown
choose a method (e.g. SNV)
read the flagged-sample count and influence plot
switch to another method (MSC, SG derivative) and compare
serves_tasks: Compare how signal pretreatment changes structure and flags
Flag unusual samples against statistical control limits
Fit a calibration model and judge its accuracy

features.name: Scree plot with component-count slider
features.general: Choose how many components to keep and see explained and cumulative variance per component
features.specific: 'PCA components' slider (2–10) plus the 'Explained variance (scree)' bar+line chart. The component count also sets the T²/Q limits and the score-axis choices
steps: drag PCA components slider
read explained bars and cumulative line
watch the effect on the outlier tab
serves_tasks: Decide how many latent components capture the variation
Flag unusual samples against statistical control limits

features.name: Interactive score plot with axis pickers, colour-by and outlier markers
features.general: Scatter samples on any two latent components, colour them by a metadata column, mark flagged samples with a distinct symbol, hover for details and toggle groups via the legend
features.specific: Score plot with X axis/Y axis selects, sidebar 'Colour points by' ((none), sample_id, group, target, _injected_outlier). Outliers and in-model points get different marker symbols, assigned by Plotly in order of appearance rather than fixed (in screens/013.webp outliers are circles, in-model points diamonds); check the legend. Plotly legend toggles hide groups
steps: choose X and Y components
choose a colour-by column
hover a point to see group, outlier status and scores
click a legend entry to hide that group
serves_tasks: See how samples group in the reduced space

features.name: Multi-component loading line plot
features.general: Overlay the loadings of selected components across all variables to see which regions of the signal drive each component
features.specific: Loading plot with 'Components to show' multiselect (defaults to the score-plot axes). Lines of loading against feature index
steps: open Components to show
add or remove PCs (Select all available)
compare loading profiles
serves_tasks: See which variables drive each component

features.name: T² vs Q influence plot with control limits and flagged table
features.general: Plot each sample's distance within the model against its distance from the model, draw statistical limits at a chosen confidence, list the flagged samples with a verdict and export them
features.specific: Hotelling's T² vs Q-residual (SPE) scatter with red dashed limits (F-distribution / Jackson-Mudholkar). Points coloured by verdict (in-model, Q outlier, T2 outlier, T2+Q outlier). Shows Flagged/Total metrics, a 'Flagged samples (suggested review)' table and 'Download diagnostics (CSV)'. Caveat: some settings flag most samples (116/120 with autoscale and 4 PCs, 94/120 with MSC and 2 PCs), so the Q limit may be miscalibrated; treat such counts with suspicion
steps: open Outlier detection tab
set the Confidence limit slider (0.90–0.99)
read the verdict colours and flagged table
download pca_outlier_diagnostics.csv
serves_tasks: Flag unusual samples against statistical control limits

screens_never_reached: Uploaded-panel analysis with all default feature columns: every run ended in a ValueError traceback (screens/046.webp, screens/049.webp, screens/051.webp) despite the 'filling with column means' warning
Score-plot box zoom: a drag on the Plotly score plot did not zoom (screens/060.webp). The legend toggle did work
not_done: Upload path with the default features crashed. After uploading example_pfas_panel.csv the app warned 'filling with column means' but raised 'array must not contain infs or NaNs' (Savitzky-Golay) and then 'Input X contains NaN' (PCA, mean-center). Removing PFOS_ng_L alone did not fix it (screens/051.webp). A reduced set (PFOA, PFHxS, PFNA, PFBS, PFOS) ran, which suggests a different column also holds missing or non-numeric values that the mean-fill does not handle

After switching to Upload CSV, the sidebar Preprocessing box showed 'autoscale', but the traceback shows the run used Savitzky-Golay 1st derivative carried over from the demo session (screens/046.webp)
With fewer than 3 feature columns the app crashes with StreamlitInvalidMinMaxError, because the PCA components slider gets min=max=2 (screens/052.webp, screens/053.webp)

The Q-residual limit looks miscalibrated in some settings. Autoscale with 4 PCs flagged 116 of 120 demo samples (screens/016.webp) and MSC with 2 PCs flagged 94 of 120 (screens/026.webp). Both are implausible at the stated 95%/99% confidence. I did not check whether the limit formula is at fault (also shown as a caveat on t7 and f5)
'target' is offered as a selectable feature column for the uploaded panel (screens/052.webp), which would leak y into X. I did not try fitting with it

In the consolidated CSV, pi_half_width is the same value (1.92) for every sample, so 'per-sample uncertainty' seems to come from residual size rather than a sample-specific interval. Seen only in the download text
Target column (y) offered only 'target' for both datasets, so I could not try a second target
I did not read the downloaded PKL model (binary), and did not load it back anywhere
I did not try 'none', 'mean-center' or 'Savitzky-Golay (smooth)' preprocessing on the synthetic data, or the Random state stepper on the PLS tab
I did not check whether the 5 Q outliers flagged under Savitzky-Golay 1st derivative (screens/028.webp) match the _injected_outlier samples
The help (?) tooltips for Data source and Feature columns returned no text on hover
